bug_semantics: The unauthenticated GET /api/artifacts handler reads the attacker-controlled id query parameter, interpolates it into the path of a Cloudflare API URL, and calls fetch with the deployment's Cloudflare KV Bearer token. URL normalization resolves ../ segments before the request is sent, so a traversal such as ../../../../../../../user/tokens/verify escapes /accounts/{account}/storage/kv/namespaces/{namespace}/values/ and reaches another Cloudflare API path with the victim token; the handler then proxies the Cloudflare response to the attacker.
flaw_origin: The flaw originated in the initial artifact-sharing feature commit 421bf33c0e033ae5ab51f08902d9aa420f5b3f65, which created app/api/artifact/route.ts and in the same commit added the user-controlled id, the direct URL interpolation, the privileged Authorization header, the outbound fetch, and response proxying. Later type, TTL, and artifact-to-artifacts rename commits preserved that mechanism and are not introducers.
ai_marker: No AI marker. The raw BIC commit object (`git cat-file commit 421bf33c0e033ae5ab51f08902d9aa420f5b3f65`) has author and committer `lloydzhou <lloydzhou@qq.com>`, one parent, and only the message `save artifact content to cloudflare workers kv`; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: First-party report https://github.com/ChatGPTNextWeb/NextChat/issues/6741 (still open, created 2026-04-07) identifies the unvalidated id interpolation in app/api/artifacts/route.ts, demonstrates seven ../ segments reaching /user/tokens/verify with the configured Bearer credential, lists affected versions <= v2.16.1, and states patched versions: none. Its linked first-party disclosure is https://gist.github.com/YLChen-007/43252d45d75e8bdd2d45136fd6ffe8a5.

In the assigned clone, `git show 421bf33c0e033ae5ab51f08902d9aa420f5b3f65:app/api/artifact/route.ts` shows the newly created GET branch obtaining `id` from searchParams, calling `fetch(storeUrl(id), { headers: storeHeaders(), method: "GET" })`, and returning the upstream body/status/headers. The same new file defines storeUrl as the Cloudflare namespace `/values/${key}` URL and storeHeaders as `Authorization: Bearer ${serverConfig.cloudflareKVApiKey}`.

`git log -L 52,63:app/api/artifacts/route.ts` traces the current GET block through d8afd1af88038d859b322fd55773c31d2cb6c4db and ab9f5382b280d3c99a62c93fac0c650f89802221 to its /dev/null addition in 421bf33c0e033ae5ab51f08902d9aa420f5b3f65. `git log --all -S 'const id = req?.nextUrl?.searchParams?.get("id")' -- app/api/artifact/route.ts app/api/artifacts/route.ts` returns only 421bf33c0e033ae5ab51f08902d9aa420f5b3f65 as the adding commit. The later d8afd1af88038d859b322fd55773c31d2cb6c4db rewrite from `storeUrl(id as string)` to `${storeUrl()}/values/${id}` is semantically equivalent and therefore not the BIC.

Direct parent verification: `git ls-tree -r --name-only 1ecefd88f741a22e83029a33d42232b69e27dddd -- app/api/artifact/route.ts app/api/artifacts/route.ts` produces no output, while `git show --stat 421bf33c0e033ae5ab51f08902d9aa420f5b3f65` records app/api/artifact/route.ts as a new 54-line file. Thus the direct parent lacks both the endpoint and its vulnerable lines.

Release boundary verification: `git describe --tags --abbrev=0 421bf33c0e033ae5ab51f08902d9aa420f5b3f65^` returns v2.13.1; `git ls-tree -r --name-only v2.13.1 -- app/api/artifact/route.ts app/api/artifacts/route.ts` is empty; the same ls-tree command at v2.14.0 returns app/api/artifacts/route.ts. `git tag --contains 421bf33c0e033ae5ab51f08902d9aa420f5b3f65 --sort=version:refname` returns every release from v2.14.0 through v2.16.1. Tag commits are v2.13.1=e079f1b31ab8cfb262a37e7ddf8ab0bf03a35464, v2.14.0=8b513537b7e9755ec3ede1de30a791fd579ecedc, and v2.16.1=557a2cce357749c6fb3176d42e03ff6f7de4d355.

No closing fix exists in the validated public history. `git show v2.16.1:app/api/artifacts/route.ts` still contains the vulnerable `${storeUrl()}/values/${id}` fetch with storeHeaders. `git log --all -- app/api/artifact/route.ts app/api/artifacts/route.ts` has no changes after the 2024-07-26 rename 6737f016f5c3d4ddc01a7b29ebb3b5df17138b96. At current origin/main HEAD defdcdb55d850cd12c4c657eb83729fd66e215c0 (2026-08-11), the checked-in route still contains the same vulnerable GET branch, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are justified nulls.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file commit 421bf33c0e033ae5ab51f08902d9aa420f5b3f65` prints tree cf2da5143533f6b672af14dcd9a5946d62e997d9, parent 1ecefd88f741a22e83029a33d42232b69e27dddd, author/committer lloydzhou <lloydzhou@qq.com>, and the one-line message, with no trailers. The GitHub commit object at https://github.com/ChatGPTNextWeb/NextChat/commit/421bf33c0e033ae5ab51f08902d9aa420f5b3f65 likewise attributes it to lloydzhou and shows a direct single-parent commit, not a merge or reconstructable squash aggregate.
reasoning: The exploit requires one coherent feature-level mistake: treating an untrusted path component as safe while forwarding a privileged Cloudflare credential and response. Commit 421bf33c0e033ae5ab51f08902d9aa420f5b3f65 is the smallest real source commit because it first adds every element of that attack path, and its immediate parent has no artifact API route. Later edits only adjust types, storage layout, TTL behavior, or rename the route. The flaw is present from v2.14.0 through the latest tagged release v2.16.1 and remains on current main; consequently there is no fix commit or fixed-version boundary to record. The BIC commit object has an ordinary human identity and no allowed AI provenance signal, so the correct BIC-only verdict is NOT_AI despite the vulnerability remaining unpatched.
remaining_gap: Unpatched in public history as of origin/main defdcdb55d850cd12c4c657eb83729fd66e215c0 (2026-08-11); therefore no fix SHA, direct-fix SHA, patched release, or closing version boundary exists to identify. No causal or AI-attribution evidence gap remains for the NOT_AI verdict.
